subject: English
passage: Born in Martinique to a family with roots in both the French Antilles and West Africa, Henry Dubois moved to Paris as a young man, and his verse drama draws on traditions from many shores: French neoclassical theater, Caribbean Creole oral poetry, Yoruba ritual storytelling, and the lyrical surrealism of early twentieth-century Parisian writers. In his 1962 masterpiece The Salt Thresholds, Dubois weaves these influences into a voice so idiosyncratic that it resists efforts to interpret his work through the lens of nationality or cultural inheritance. Poets, he argued, should pursue a singular voice of their own, even as they listen attentively to the heritages and communities that have shaped them.
prompt: Which quotation from a literary critic most directly challenges the underlined claim in the text?

choices.A: "Although several Caribbean and West African poetic traditions favor call-and-response cadences, the rhythmic patterns coursing through The Salt Thresholds suggest a specifically Yoruba ritual influence."
choices.B: "In The Salt Thresholds, the merging of ritual chant and neoclassical verse functions as a formal echo of the play's subject matter: a meditation on centuries of Atlantic crossings."
choices.C: "Many critics dwell on the Creole and Yoruba elements of The Salt Thresholds and Dubois's other major works to the exclusion of his clear debts to French surrealism."
choices.D: "Although The Salt Thresholds borrows surrealist imagery, it is built around alexandrine couplets and stately classical diction—hallmarks of French theatrical tradition—and thus invites reading as a French national work."

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. This critic challenges the underlined claim by arguing that The Salt Thresholds is not so idiosyncratic as to resist classification: its alexandrine couplets and classical diction allegedly 'invite reading as a French national work.' This directly contradicts the assertion that the play resists interpretation through the lens of nationality or cultural inheritance.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. This quotation supports rather than challenges the underlined claim. By describing how the play merges ritual chant and neoclassical verse to mirror centuries of Atlantic crossings, it emphasizes the very fusion of traditions that makes the work resist any single cultural classification.
